tasks.locator: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03537014 › Study Record Dates; Outcome Measures; Results › Outcome Measures
tasks.extracted: Registered 14 May 2018 (posted 25 May 2018), before the first participant (21 November 2018), with change in CAPS-5 to 18 weeks as the primary outcome; registry least-squares mean change −24.5 (95% CI −28.28 to −20.71) on MDMA vs −12.64 (−16.61 to −8.66) on placebo (modified ITT, 46 and 44).

Eligible: DSM-5 PTSD for at least 6 months and CAPS-5 of 35 or more after washout of psychiatric medicines; excluded: current alcohol and substance use disorders, personality disorders, conditions making a sympathomimetic harmful. Baseline CAPS-5 44.1 (SD 6.04); comorbid major depression 82 of 90 (91.1%); 69 (76.7%) White.

The primary outcome was a short-term one, 2 months after the last experimental session; long-term follow-up data are to be published later; blinding of participants was not formally assessed and, the authors say, was challenging and possibly led to expectation effects.

De jure MMRM: least-squares mean change in CAPS-5 −23.7 (95% CI −26.94 to −20.44) on MDMA vs −14.8 (−18.28 to −11.28) on placebo with therapy; treatment difference −8.9 (−13.70 to −4.12), P < 0.001; d = 0.7; de facto −23.7 vs −14.8, P < 0.001.

At 18 weeks, among those assessed: response 45 of 52 (86.5%) vs 29 of 42 (69.0%); loss of diagnosis 37 of 52 (71.2%) vs 20 of 42 (47.6%); remission 24 of 52 (46.2%) vs 9 of 42 (21.4%). Editors' calculation with all 53 and 51 randomized as denominators: loss of diagnosis 69.8% vs 39.2% (difference 30.6 points, 95% CI 12.4 to 48.8).

tasks.locator: Methods › Randomization and masking, 2nd and 3rd paragraphs
tasks.extracted: Outcomes rated by a central pool of independent assessors blinded to the design, visit, assignment, number of treatments and safety data, each doing one CAPS-5 per participant; participants asked to withhold their opinion on assignment; the blinding survey was given at study termination (visit 20). Assessors' guesses are not reported.

Treatment expectancy was not measured; the authors offer three observations as support for its mitigation: the groups did not separate after the first session, placebo dropouts did not all occur after the first session, and not all participants identified their treatment.

tasks.locator: Methods › Randomization, masking and bias minimization, 2nd and 3rd paragraphs
tasks.extracted: An inactive placebo was chosen with the FDA, the authors noting that low-dose MDMA had improved blinding in phase 2 but was less effective than inactive placebo; outcomes were rated by an observer-blind independent rater pool by video, and participants were told to withhold their opinion on assignment.
Lifetime MDMA use reported by 29 of 90 (32.2%), in the past 10 years by 19 (21.1%).

The review counts functional unblinding in four of six MAPS trials, with blinding maintained or partly maintained only in two trials that used low-dose MDMA as comparator; its Table 5 gives 95% correct guesses by participants in the 2011 pilot trial with an inactive placebo.
The trial's authors call blinding in psychedelic trials a tremendous challenge with no perfect solution and state that no flawless comparator exists for psychedelic-assisted therapy.

Background statement citing news reports and a JAMA piece (Jacobs, 2024; Jarow, 2024a, 2024b; Marks, 2024): the FDA rejected the application after a split vote of an independent advisory committee, whose concerns included maintaining the blind given MDMA's psychoactive effects, the sufficiency of long-term safety data, ethical concerns about therapist behaviour during the trials, the difficulty of separating the effects of MDMA from the accompanying psychotherapy, and generalizability given homogeneous samples. No vote counts are given.

tasks.locator: Entire text (standfirst, 11 paragraphs, Fig. 1 legend, competing interests)
tasks.extracted: The News & Views on the first trial does not mention blinding, expectancy, the comparison condition or any trial number; it describes the trial as showing significant efficacy and an excellent safety profile.

Describes the first phase 3 trial as randomized, double-blind and placebo-controlled, with a significant reduction in CAPS-5 score compared with placebo and as much as two thirds of the MDMA arm no longer meeting PTSD criteria after treatment (no denominator, time point or placebo-arm figure); says the safety profile appears favourable because the trial did not induce adverse events of abuse potential, suicidality or QT prolongation, without a citation. Nothing is said about whether the blind held or about expectancy.
O.A. is a principal investigator for the phase IIB and III clinical trials in the MAPS-sponsored MDMA-AT trials for PTSD; S.M. declares no conflict.

The authors write that psychedelic research appears caught in a hype bubble driven largely by media and industry interests (Yaden et al., 2022) and that major medical journals have been debated for lowering their standards for psychedelic trials (Hall and Humphreys, 2022), without applying either point to the trials they describe.

Treatment-emergent adverse events more frequent on MDMA were typically transient and mild to moderate: muscle tightness, decreased appetite, nausea, hyperhidrosis and feeling cold; transient rises in blood pressure and heart rate on MDMA; a temperature of 38.1 °C in two MDMA participants.

Adverse events at 5% or more (first experimental session to termination visit, about 18 weeks; 46 vs 44): muscle tightness 28 vs 6, decreased appetite 24 vs 5, nausea 14 vs 5, hyperhidrosis 10 vs 1, feeling cold 9 vs 3, mydriasis 7 vs 0, restlessness 7 vs 0, nystagmus 6 vs 0, bruxism 6 vs 1, blood pressure increased 5 vs 0; suicidal ideation 21 vs 21; serious events 0 vs 2.

Serious adverse events: three in two placebo participants (suicidal behaviour; suicidal ideation leading to self-hospitalization), none on MDMA; suicidality events of special interest 3 (6.5%) on MDMA vs 5 (11.4%) on placebo; cardiac events that could indicate QT prolongation 0 vs 1; abuse potential 0 vs 0.

Suicidal ideation at baseline in 17 of 46 (37%) on MDMA and 14 of 44 (32%) on placebo; during the study the number with ideation never exceeded baseline, and serious ideation (C-SSRS 4 or 5) occurred almost entirely on placebo.
Expected effects of MDMA, such as euphoria, stimulation and feelings of closeness, were not solicited as adverse events, to avoid biasing adverse-event collection.

tasks.locator: Methods › Statistics and reproducibility, 10th paragraph; Discussion, 10th paragraph

tasks.extracted: Adverse events counted from the first experimental session to the last integration session, severity graded by the site physician; except for serious events, relatedness to the drug was not assessed, to preserve blinding; events were attributed to MDMA when more than 10% and at least twice as frequent as on placebo.

tasks.locator: Drug pricing: a critical policy concern, 1st and 2nd paragraphs (left column)
